record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L × L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?

evidence.quote: Take a square region R of size n × n in the torus ... The Hamiltonian is then defined by translating hR, H = Στ τ(hR) ... The basic open question here is the following
Question 1 Which are the minimal requirements on A and the minimal size of R under which one can guarantee that the given PEPS is the unique ground state of H and in addition H is gapped?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d,D\ge 2$ and $L\ge 2$. A translationally invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on the $L\times L$ torus is determined by a single local tensor
$$A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D},$$
with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ associated to the four lattice directions. Placing a copy of $A$ at every vertex of the torus and contracting all virtual indices along edges shared by neighbouring sites yields the PEPS vector $|\Psi_A\rangle\in(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L^2}$.

For a square region $R\subset\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L$ of size $n\times n$, let $\mathcal{V}_R:(\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4n}\to(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$ be the linear map obtained by contracting the $n^2$ copies of $A$ inside $R$, viewing the $4n$ virtual indices on $\partial R$ as input and the $n^2$ physical indices as output. Let $\Pi_R$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $\mathrm{Range}(\mathcal{V}_R)\subset(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$, and define the local term $h_R:=\mathbb{1}-\Pi_R\ge 0$. The parent Hamiltonian is
$$H \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L}\tau(h_R),$$
where $\tau$ acts on operators by lattice translation. By construction $H\ge 0$ and $H|\Psi_A\rangle=0$.

Problem. Determine the weakest possible conditions on the tensor $A$ together with the smallest possible side length $n$ of the square region $R$ such that, for all sufficiently large $L$, the following two properties simultaneously hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|\Psi_A\rangle$ is the unique ground state of $H$ (so that the kernel of $H$ is one-dimensional);
\item[(ii)] $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground state that is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $L$.
\end{enumerate}
Identify the minimal hypotheses on $A$ (e.g. injectivity-type, normality-type, or strictly weaker algebraic/spectral conditions on the transfer operator of $A$) and the minimal $n$ for which (i) and (ii) can be guaranteed.
artifact.status_search_result: Sufficient conditions exist (e.g. injectivity gives uniqueness; normality plus additional assumptions give a gap in 1D, and partial 2D results exist), and generalizations such as semi-injective PEPS extend the uniqueness class. However, identifying the minimal conditions on the tensor and the minimal region size that simultaneously guarantee uniqueness and a uniform spectral gap of the parent Hamiltonian on a 2D torus remains an open problem; in 2D the gap can fail even under injectivity, and no minimal characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: PEPS as unique ground states of local Hamiltonians
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs parent Hamiltonians and gives injectivity-type conditions under which a PEPS is the unique ground state.
status_evidence.claim: Injectivity is a known sufficient condition for uniqueness, but minimality is not established.

status_evidence.title: A generalization of the injectivity condition for PEPS (semi-injective)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces semi-injective PEPS extending injective PEPS, with parent Hamiltonians having them as unique ground states.
status_evidence.claim: Work continues to weaken sufficient conditions, indicating the minimal conditions remain unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Frustration Free Gapless Hamiltonians for Matrix Product States
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that injective/normal MPS/PEPS parent Hamiltonians can be gapless in higher-dimensional or related settings.
status_evidence.claim: Gap is not automatic from uniqueness conditions in 2D, so minimal gap conditions are open.
